item.title: 辨析三个和 “忧郁” 有关的近义词：“melancholy”、“sombre” 和 “poignant”
item.description:
内容简介

你也喜欢看艺术展、读小说吗？如果你仔细观察画作或小说的英文介绍，可能会发现一些经常反复出现的形容词——“melancholy”、“sombre” 和 “poignant”。这三个单词常常被用来描述那些 “带有忧郁基调，让人感到悲伤或惆怅” 的作品。那么，它们之间有什么区别？又可以在哪些语境中使用呢？跟主持人步理和 Phil 一起学习这些颇具 “艺术气息” 的单词吧。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。This is Question and Answer of the Week, where we answer your questions about English language, culture and life. I'm Buli. Phil's here to help me answer a question about sad but similar words.

Phil
Let's not get too sad yet. Let's hear the question.

Question
你好，我平时喜欢看艺术展，然后就会发现一些单词在展览上有非常高的 “出镜率”，经常出现在艺术作品的简介中。比如，“melancholy”、“sombre” 和 “poignant” 就经常用来形容那些比较忧郁、暗色调的画作。我偶尔也会在小说里见到这些看起来文学性很强的单词，但还是不太清楚它们具体都想描述出什么样的感觉，请问可以介绍一下吗？

Buli
So, we're looking at words that we can use to describe sadness in art.

这位听众提出的问题确实有些 “忧郁”，因为 “melancholy”、“sombre” 和 “poignant” 形容的通常都是有些愁苦的负面情感。不过也正如问题中所说，如果我们经常观赏或阅读一些美术和文学作品，那么就很可能会见到它们。

Phil
Yes. And, as is so often the case with these questions, we can sometimes use these words to describe the same thing, but they do have some subtle differences.

Buli
Yes, let's start by listening to some examples.

Phil, you look a bit sad. What are you thinking about?

Phil
It's this book. There's this scene that's so poignant, I can't stop thinking about it! It's sad, but it's also really moving. I really feel for the characters.

Buli
Wow, that's a very sombre looking cover – all dark colours and serious-looking people. It's not a comedy, I guess?

Phil
Oh no, definitely not! It's a bit heavy. Look at this quote on the back: 'An air of melancholy runs through the whole novel.' That's not wrong – it's all about loss and how that can affect someone's life. Do you want to read it?

Buli
Um… no, thanks. I really need something that's fun to read today.

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在刚才的对话中，我和 Phil 使用了问题中提到的三个单词来描述一本书的外观、内容和带给人的感觉。下面我们就来具体讲一讲这三个单词之间有哪些区别和共同点。Let's start with 'melancholy'.

Phil
Yes. The first thing to note is grammatical. 'Melancholy' is both a noun and an adjective. You can have 'an air of melancholy', but also you can have 'a melancholy atmosphere'. Melancholy is often a sadness that lasts for a long time and often without a clear reason.

Buli
Yes. We often use it to describe a mood or an atmosphere. It can be linked to nostalgia, longing or yearning.

“Melancholy” 这个词和另外两者之间最大的区别就是它既是一个形容词，也是一个名词。它描述的是那种 “长久的、痛苦的忧伤”，像是 “对过去事物的怀念、渴望而不得的想念或者遥不可及的向往” 等等。比如，我们可以用 “a melancholy atmosphere” 来描述 “忧伤愁闷的气氛”，也可以用 “a deep melancholy” 来表示 “一种深深的惆怅”。

So, what about 'sombre'?

Phil
OK, 'sombre' is an adjective. It means 'sad' or 'serious'. A sombre mood, or a sombre atmosphere could be the same as melancholy, but it doesn't have the same idea of something lasting a long time.

You can have a sombre event or hear sombre news. You can have a sombre expression. We also talk about sombre colours – those are dark, serious colours.

Buli
So, 'sombre' is more connected to seriousness than a burst of emotion.

形容词 “sombre” 可以理解为 “庄重而阴沉的，沉痛的，肃穆的” 等等。当用它来形容周遭的气氛时，表达出的意境和 “melancholy” 有些相似。不过，“sombre” 更强调那种 “在当下的、严肃而沉重的忧郁和悲伤”。此外，我们还可以用 “sombre” 来形容颜色，特别是那些 “阴暗的，厚重的” 颜色。

你或许已经注意到了，“sombre” 这个词有两种拼法。就像 “centre（中心）” 和 “theatre（剧院）” 一样，在英国，人们会把它拼写为由 “-re” 结尾；而在一些其它地方，人们可能会用 “-er” 结尾。

Phil
A word that really is all about emotion is 'poignant'. Something that is poignant, makes you feel a particular way, usually something related to sadness. A poignant scene in a film moves you emotionally, so we can also describe it as 'moving'.

Buli
是的。在这三个单词中，“poignant” 和人的感情最直接相关。如果我们说 “something is poignant”，意思就是 “某样事物能强烈地激起人的情绪，特别是悲伤的、伤感的或者酸楚的情绪，令人动容”。不过要注意的是，“poignant” 并不一定意味着带来的感情是负面的。当我们被激起了希望、怜悯或者感动时，也可以用 “poignant” 来形容那些激起我们感情的事物。

Phil
Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: “预约” 和 “预购”：英语怎么说？
英语中的 “diminutives（爱称词）”：“sarnie” 和 “telly” 是怎么来的？
item.description:
内容简介

穿上 “jammies”，坐在 “telly” 前，再来几块 “choccy biccies”…… 可别以为这些听起来像 “咿呀学语” 的单词就不算英语！其实，它们都属于英语中的 “diminutives（爱称词）”，是人们在日常口语中用来称呼身边常见事物的昵称。听节目，跟主持人步理和 Georgie 一起学习几个在英国十分常见的单词爱称，并了解它们是如何从原先的单词变化而来的吧。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。This is Question and Answer of the Week, where we answer your questions about English language, culture and life. I'm Buli and I'm here with Georgie. How are you?

Georgie
Hmm, I'm not feeling great today, Buli. But don't worry. I've got a choccy biccy in my bag that will cheer me up. And later, my plan is to put my jammies on, make myself a cuppa and stick the telly on. A perfect evening. How are you?

Buli
Georgie… what language are you speaking?

Georgie
I'm speaking English, Buli!

Buli
Hmm, OK. Well, I have a feeling we're going to learn some Britishisms. Shall we hear the question?

Georgie
Let's do it.

Question
British people have many nicknames for everyday stuff, which I find somehow very cute, like 'sarnie' for sandwich, 'telly' for TV. Are there any other commonly used ones like these that I should probably learn?

Buli
这位听众注意到，英语，特别是在英式英语中，人们会给不少日常生活中的小物件起  “小名”。比如，人们会把 “sandwich（三明治）” 叫做 “sarnie”。在本期节目中，我们就来介绍几个常见物品在英语中的 “爱称”。

Georgie
Are you sure you didn't write this question, Buli?

Buli
Ha! It does sound like something I would ask! I almost regret not mentioning it earlier myself, and I would really like to hear the answer! So, Georgie, what can you tell us?

Georgie
Well, what this listener is talking about here are called 'diminutives'. These are words shortened to sound cuter or more affectionate. 'Sarnie' is a cute, shortened name for 'sandwich'. 'Telly' is a shortened version of 'television'.

Buli
Right. 诸如 “sarnie（三明治）” 和 “telly（电视）” 等小词在英语中也被称为 “diminutives（爱称）”。在英语中，特别是在英国，人们会出于方便、简洁或对某些东西的喜爱而在称呼它们时使用简短的爱称。久而久之，一些朗朗上口的爱称就被保留了下来，并且这些爱称还往往有一定的变形规律。

For example, I can see here that we cut off the end of the word 'television' and 'sandwich', and add the /i:/ sound, either spelt with 'ie' or 'y' – 'telly' and 'sarnie'.

Georgie
Exactly. Now, do you remember when I said I had a 'choccy biccy' in my bag? What do you think that means?

Buli
Choccy biccy… I think 'choccy' means chocolate, but I'm not sure about 'biccy'.

Georgie
Biscuit! I've got a chocolate biscuit in my bag – a choccy biccy. We also sometimes shorten 'vegetables' to 'veggies'. Make sure to eat enough veggies!

Buli
If they are actually that cute, I will! 除了 “sarnie”，还有不少食物都有自己的爱称。比如，“chocolate（巧克力）” 会被称为 “choccy”，“biscuit（饼干）” 可以被称为 “biccy”，而 “vegetables（蔬菜）” 则经常被人们叫做 “veggies”。我们可以注意到，这些爱称通常只保留单词的前半部分，再加上 “ie” 或 “y” 等发长元音 /i:/ 的后缀。

Georgie, you also said you're going to put your 'jammies' on later. What does that mean? I hope you are not pouring jam all over yourself.

Georgie
Of course not! 'Jammies' is short for 'pyjamas'. As you can see, they don't all follow the rule of cutting off just the end of the word and adding the /i:/ sound. With this one, we cut off the first syllable too. 'Pyjamas' becomes just 'jammies'.

Buli
是的。除了上面提到的这些爱称，还有一些爱称并不完全符合同样的规律，比如十分常见的爱称 “cuppa（一杯茶）”。Georgie, what's a 'cuppa'? And why isn't it a 'cuppy'?

Georgie
'A cuppa' is short for 'a cup of tea'. That's because when we say 'a cup of tea' quickly, we don't pronounce the word 'of', it becomes a schwa sound – a cuppa tea.

Buli
Right. And then you just take off 'tea' at the end, and it becomes 'a cuppa'. I like it!

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习英语里常见的 “diminutives（爱称）”。

Georgie
OK, Buli. Why don't you have a go with these diminutives then. Let's hear it.

Buli
OK. Well, I've been having far too many choccy biccies lately. I need to get more veggies in my diet. If I eat more veggies, I can reward myself with a cuppa in front of the telly.

Georgie
Great! OK. Now, time to recap.

Buli
英语母语者，特别是英国人，经常用 “diminutives（爱称）” 来称呼日常生活中的小物件。其中，大部分爱称都会保留原本单词的前半部分，再加上以长元音 /i:/ 结尾的后缀 “ie” 或 “y”。比如，“veggies（蔬菜）”、“choccy（巧克力）” 或者 “telly（电视）”。但也有一些爱称并不完全遵循这一规则，比如， “jammies（睡衣）” 就是 “pyjamas” 的爱称，而 “a cuppa” 则是 “a cup of tea” 的爱称。

Georgie
It's important to remember that while these are quite common in British English, they aren't necessarily common in other varieties.

And don't forget that if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你也可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是“BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Georgie
Goodbye!

item.title: “Picture”、“image”、“photo” 和 “graph”：这些 “图” 一样吗？
item.description:
内容简介

手机拍的 “图”、画布上绘制的 “图”、以及数学公式在坐标系中对应的 “图”……这些不同类型的 “图”，在英语里的说法一样吗？又该如何区分使用 “picture”、“image”、“photo” 和 “graph” 呢？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Phil 一起辨析这四个表示 "图，图像” 的单词之间的区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。This is Question and Answer of the Week, where we answer your questions about English language, culture and life. I'm Buli. Phil's here to help me look at a graphical question.

Phil
That sounds interesting. Let's hear the question.

Question
我一直都分不清在英语里 “photo”、“picture”、“image” 和 “graph” 这几个词到底哪个是 “照片”、哪个是 “图像”，如果有比较清晰的区分方式，请问可以辨析一下吗？

Phil
It's a good question because these words can overlap, but some of them have got very specific meanings. Let's try and break it down.

Buli
没错。其实在日常生活中，这几个词被人们互换使用的情况确实不少。比如，“picture” 和 “image” 的含义就非常宽泛，可以指代各种各样的 “图像，影像，照片” 等等。不过，“photo” 和 “graph” 的用法就相对比较具体了。让我们先来听一段对话。

Phil
Oh, Buli, those pictures look great. What are they?

Buli
Oh, I was just looking through some photos from my holiday. I need to work out what to save. I can't fit that many image files on my phone.

Phil
You've got a load of graphs there, surely you don't need those.

Buli
I can't delete those! They are my 'cheat sheets' for next week's work presentation.

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在辨析四个和 “照片，图片” 有关的近义词 “picture”、“image”、“photo” 和 “graph”。

Phil
So, as Buli said, 'picture' and 'image' are more general. You can take a picture with a camera, but you can also paint one or draw one by hand.

Buli
You can even picture something in your mind. When we use it as verb, we are usually talking about something you imagine in your head.

正如我们之前提到的，单词 “picture” 可以用来表示各种各样的 “照片，图片，影像，图画” 等等。 “Picture” 还可以用作动词，意思是 “想象一个东西的样子”。

Phil
'Image' is also general but is a bit more formal and technical. It's something that you look at, and like picture, it can also be something that you imagine. I said that it's technical, we usually use 'image' to talk about digital files, so you can have 'image files' as opposed to 'video files' or 'music files', for example. And in a hospital, you might have an imaging department that takes x-rays or scans, for example.

Buli
Yes. And we can also talk about 'moving images' that you might see on a TV, phone or cinema screen.

虽然也能表示广义上的各种 “图像，影像，照片”，但单词 “image” 的含义和 “picture” 略有不同。通常来讲，人们会在更专业、技术性更强的场合用 “image” 来指代某张 “图” 或 “图像”。比如，去医院做检查时扫描仪记录的影像等等。此外，在描述手机、电脑等电子介质上存储的影像资料时，“image（图片）” 也经常和 “video（视频）” 相对应。

Phil
'Photo' is much more specific. Photos don't move, and you make them with a camera. Remember we do still also call photos 'pictures' or 'images'. Sometimes we call them 'still images' to emphasise the fact that they are not moving.

Buli
是的，“photo” 指的就是 “照片”，也就是 “用相机拍摄的、固定不动的图片”。

Phil
The last one that we are going to talk about is 'graph'. A graph is an image, but it's very different to a photo. It's a way of presenting data, usually numbers.

Buli
And they are not taken by a camera. 单词 “graph” 的意思是 “图表，图形”。它通常指的是那些 “用数字、文字、线条等元素来展示信息的图表”，所以其实和 “照片” 这个含义还是相去甚远的。

Phil, there are also different types of graphs, aren't there?

Phil
Yes. And we sometimes call them 'charts'. Line graphs, bar charts, pie charts... The line, bar, pie segments, or other images are all different formats to represent numbers to make them easier to understand.

Buli
Oh, that reminded me, I need to finish making my charts for the presentation after this!

最后让我们来复习一下。“Picture”、“image”、“photo” 和 “graph” 都是和 “图，图像” 这个含义有关的单词。其中，“picture” 和 “image” 都可以在广义上指代各种 “图像，图片，照片，影像” 等等。不过，“image” 通常用在更专业和技术性的场合，比如，医学影像等等。“Photo” 则特指 “用相机拍摄的图片”。“Graph” 指的则是 “用数字、文字和线条等元素绘制而成的图表、图形”，有时也可以被称为 “chart”，比如，“line graph（折线图）”、“pie chart（饼图）”、“bar chart（柱状图）” 等等。

Phil
Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: 五个都可以表示 “歌曲” 的单词，有什么区别?
item.description:
内容简介

同样表示 “一首歌”，英语里却有许多不同的说法。不同单词对应不同的场合、音乐形式和谈论音乐的角度。比如，“tune” 和 “melody” 侧重描述 “曲调，旋律”，而 “track” 则多指专辑中的  “一首曲目” 或音频剪辑软件中的 “音轨”。听节目，跟主持人步理和 Becca 一起辨析 “music”、“tune”、“melody”、“track” 和 “sound” 这五个单词的区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。We are here to answer your questions about English language, culture and life. I'm Buli, and I'm with Becca, who is here to help me answer this week's question. Hi Becca, how are you?

Becca
Hey, Buli, I'm well thanks. I'm in a pretty good mood because the cafe is playing some relaxing jazz music.

Buli
Oh cool, I love their chill playlist. Hey, that's got me thinking about the question that we've just received. It's about how we talk about songs and music. 一位听众向我们发来了这样的问题：

Question
Hi. I found your programme about different words to describe a picture very useful! Could you please also help me learn the difference between these words to describe a song as well: 'music', 'tune', 'sound', 'track'. How are they used differently when talking about a piece of music? Thank you!

Buli
在英语中，经常会出现多个单词和同一个概念相联系的情况。比如，这位听众就提到了，当人们在谈论一首 “歌” 的时候，会使用诸如 “music”、“tune”、“track” 等不同的单词。在本期节目中，我们就来看看这些单词之间有什么区别。

Becca
Oh, the programme music is a bit loud. Would you mind turning it down, Buli?

Buli
Sure. But if I turn it down too much, you might not be able to hear the melody.

Becca
I suppose so. Why don't I just hum the tune instead? [Becca sings]

Buli
Hmm, when you hum it, it doesn't have the same energetic sound.

Becca
OK, what about this? [Becca sings]

Buli
OK, OK. It's a bit better, but it sounds a bit like that track from that popstar you like. We don't want to get in trouble for plagiarism!

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Becca 正在辨析几个能够用来描述一首 “歌” 的单词：“music”、“tune”、“melody”、“sound” 和 “track”。

Shall we talk about these different musical terms, Becca?

Becca
Yes! We'll start with 'music'. 'Music' is the general term. Music can be in the form of a live performance – with people playing music in front of you, or it can be recorded audio. For example, the cafe was playing recorded jazz music.

Buli
单词 “music” 的意思就是 “音乐”。它既可以宽泛地指 “音乐” 这种艺术形式，也可以指 “a piece of music（一首具体的音乐作品）”，或者任何正在播放的音乐或歌曲等等。

For example, when you asked me to turn down the programme music, you meant the volume of it as a whole.

Becca
Indeed. Now, a 'tune' and a 'melody' are quite similar. They refer more to the rhythm of the music rather than the lyrics or the words. That's why we can hum a tune or a melody. We can also say a piece of music or song is 'out of tune' if the pitch – that is how high or low a sound is – is wrong.

Buli
是的。“Tune” 和 “melody” 通常指的是歌曲的 “曲调，旋律”。比如，如果我们想说一首歌的 “旋律特别容易让人记住，甚至听着有些上头”，就可以说这首歌 “has a catchy tune”。再比如，当我们在夸奖一首歌 “has a beautiful melody” 的时候，意思就是这首歌的 “旋律非常优美”。

除此之外，有时人们也会在口语中用 “tune” 来表示 “一首歌”，特别是现代的流行歌曲。

Now, what about sound?

Becca
Sound is the character or quality of the audio, like the tone, style, or production. Like when I hummed the programme music, you said it didn't have the same energetic sound. And we'll often talk about a musician's sound to mean their overall musical identity. For example, that popstar I love has a very upbeat sound – the music she plays and sings makes me want to dance!

Buli
So, we can say that 'sound' is about the style, but not the structure of a song?

Becca
Exactly.

Buli
单词 “sound” 的意思就是 “声音”。在谈论音乐时，人们通常会用 “sound” 来指代歌曲的 “品质，质量” 或者一名歌手的 “声音质感”，它更像是声音给人的感觉而不是其中具体的歌词、曲调、节奏等元素。就比如，我们可以说一首歌 “has a powerful sound（十分具有力量感，震撼人心）”。

And lastly, how is 'track' different?

Becca
A track is a recording of a specific piece of audio. In everyday language, a track usually means one recorded song, especially in digital contexts. I might say that 'track 3 of the new album is my favourite', or that 'the playlist is full of great tracks'.

Buli
没错。和其它几个单词相比，“track” 所指的对象更为具体，通常描述的是 “录制在一张专辑里、一张光盘或者一盒磁带等介质上的一首歌曲”。在音乐的制作阶段，“track” 还可以指音频中 “一个独立的、可以单独调整的音频轨道”，比如，单独用于录制吉他、钢琴或人声的 “音轨”。

Becca
Yes! Now let's finish this programme, Buli, because I want to play you a new track by my favourite popstar. I think you'll like the sound!

And remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!

item.title: 如何用好 “double negatives（双重否定）”
item.description:
内容简介

当别人问你 “How are you?” 时，你会如何回答？在英国，除了 “I'm well” 和 “I'm fine” 之外，很多人还会用 “not bad(还不错)” 来回答，而这种表达方式就属于 “double negatives（双重否定）”。与直接使用肯定句或否定句相比，双重否定有哪些独特的含义和用法？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Georgie 一探究竟。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。This is Question and Answer of the Week, where we answer your questions about English language, culture and life. I'm Buli and Georgie's here to help me answer a question. How are you?

Georgie
Not bad, not bad. You?

Buli
Just 'not bad'?

Georgie
Well, I've not been unhappy…

Buli
Georgie, are you happy or not?

Georgie
I'm fine! How are you?

Buli
I'm pretty good, thanks! But, Georgie, why weren't you more direct when I asked you how you were?

Georgie
Ah, well that's because in English, especially in British English, sometimes we prefer to be more cautious with our statements.

Buli
I don't disagree. Shall we hear this week's question?

Georgie
That's not the worst idea!

Buli
What?!

Georgie
I mean… That's a good idea! Let's hear it now.

Question
我觉得英语里的双重否定句，甚至是多重否定句的真实含义非常难以识别，特别是在口语对话中经常让我来不及反应。请问英语里为什么会用双重否定句呢？它会暗示出特别的意思吗？有什么方法或者窍门能更快地识别双重否定句的正确含义吗？

Buli
这位听众提到的 “双重否定句” 在英语里被称为 “double negatives”。双重否定句中，往往至少含有一个否定词 “no” 或者 “not”，以及一个具有否定意义的单词，比如 “nobody（没有人）”、“bad（不好的，坏的）” 或者 “unhappy（不开心的）”。不过，“双重否定” 并不一定就是 “肯定”。在本期节目中，咱们就来看看在英语里人们是如何使用双重否定句的。

Right, Georgie. Let's jump straight into some of the examples you used at the beginning. When I asked you how you were, you said 'not bad'. We've got a negative word there – 'bad' and made it a double negative with 'not'. So, does 'not bad' mean 'good'?

Georgie
Hmm, not quite. 'Not bad' is not 'good'. It means something in the middle – quite good. British people use this response to 'How are you?' a lot. In the same way, you might hear 'not uncommon', which means quite common.

Buli
Right, and you also said you are 'not unhappy', which I guess means fairly happy, but not very happy.

Georgie
Exactly. Using double negatives in this way helps us to not make strong claims and be less direct. Next, let's look at when you said, 'I don't disagree'. Compare 'I agree' with 'I don't disagree'. The first is stronger than the second. 'I don't disagree' could be followed by 'but'. It's a softer claim.

Buli
Well, I don't disagree, but I do think it's better to be more direct. It's easier to understand!

在英语中，特别是在英国，人们会用双重否定句来让自己的说法听上去不那么绝对。比如，在被问到自己对一件事的想法时，比起直接说 “I don't agree” 或者 “I agree”，用 “I don't disagree” 听起来就更加温和。同时，我们也可以用 “I don't disagree, but…” 来引出自己的建议和一些小想法，这样往往听上去也会更容易让人接受。

Now, you said listening to the question was 'not the worst idea'. What did you mean by that?

Georgie
I meant 'That's a pretty good idea.' British English speakers sometimes like using understatement. These are often more positive than you expect. For example, 'not bad' can often mean pretty good, in a surprising way.

Buli
That's true. 在英式英语中，人们还常常会选择双重否定句作为一种低调的评价方式，也就是 “understatement”。就比如，如果一个人对你说 “that's not a bad idea”，那么对方的意思很可能并不是 “这主意还不赖”，而其实是 “这主意非常不错”，并且往往还带有一种惊讶和出乎意料的感觉。

Georgie
In terms of a tip to react to double negatives more quickly, I think it's about hearing lots of examples and just getting used to them. Try not to think that a negative plus a negative automatically means something positive. Ask yourself these questions: Is this speaker being polite? Are they softening criticism? Expressing understatement? Avoiding certainty? The answer is often 'yes' to at least one of those if they are using a double negative.

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习英语里双重否定句的用法。

Georgie
I want to share one more example of when British English speakers use double negatives to be indirect. Ask me a question with a suggestion, Buli.

Buli
Sure. Would you like to get lunch together in our break?

Georgie
Well, I wouldn't say no…

Buli
Right. So, is that a 'yes'?

Georgie
It's not a 'no'!

Buli
Georgie…

Georgie
Let's go for lunch later. I'm in. But first, it wouldn't be a bad idea for you to recap.

Buli
Ah, I see! Well, I can't say that's untrue.

最后，让我们来总结一下。在英语中，特别是在英式英语中，人们经常会用双重否定句来避免语气过于直截了当或者说法太过绝对。此外，英语母语者，特别是英国人，也经常用双重否定来让自己相对明显的看法或态度显得更为低调，甚至是略微掩盖自己的惊讶和惊叹之情。比如，“this is not a bad little restaurant” 的意思其实可能是 “这家餐厅竟然还挺不错的”。因此，我们在理解双重否定句时，除了多听多练，也要学会识别沟通交流中的文字以外的信息。比如，对方的语气是积极的还是有所保留的？肢体动作和表情如何变化？他们有没有提出其它观点或想法？这些观察都能帮助我们更好地理解双重否定的含义。

Georgie
Don't forget that if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你也可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Georgie
Goodbye!

item.title: 受了点小伤，怎么用英语说最准确？
item.description:
内容简介

在英语中，人们会用 “cuts and scrapes” 来统称各种 “小磕小碰”。在日常生活中，难免会有撞到头、划伤胳膊、切到手指的时侯，而英语里也有许多更准确的词来描述不同类型的小伤。在本期节目中，主持人步理和 Becca 将分享六个描述 “受了点小伤” 时的常用单词，并讲解它们的地道用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。We are here to answer your questions about English language, culture and life. I'm Buli, and I'm with Becca, who is here to help me answer this week's question. Hi Becca, how are you?

Becca
Oh, Buli, I'm so clumsy. I was walking while looking down at my phone, and I bumped into a glass door! Is there a bruise on my head?

Buli
Oh no! Are you OK? Let me see… Ah, I think you'll be OK. That actually fits perfectly with today's question! 在本期节目中我们将要回答的问题是这样的：

Question 
我最近想要和别人描述我受的一点小伤，但除了 “wound” 没有想到其它特别合适的词。我知道 “cuts and scrapes” 好像也可以指各种小伤，但能请教一下，其它生活中不小心受的伤还有哪些对应的英语单词吗？

Becca
I really hope I don't get a bruise though. My skin bruises so easily, I'm like a peach!

Buli
Your head is a bit red. I think a bump may be appearing! Where did this happen?

Becca
You know the entrance to the cafe on the 7th floor?

Buli
I know it! I tripped over there in my first few weeks of work! It was so embarrassing. Luckily, I only scratched my knee.

Becca
Oh dear, Buli! Did anyone see?

Buli
Only a few people. My pride was wounded more than my knee, to be honest.

Becca
Yeah, I bet! That reminds me of the time I tripped and fell off a bus on my way to a job interview. A few people saw, but I was more embarrassed to turn up to my interview with scrapes on my arms from the stones on the pavement.

Buli
Oh no. Did you get the job though?

Becca
I didn't. I was cut deep that day. I didn't go to any job interviews for like a month!

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在刚才的对话中，我和 Becca 使用了许多跟  “injure（受伤)” 和 “wound（伤口）” 有关的表达。如果你在生活中也容易犯点小马虎，经常小小地伤到自己一下，那么本期节目的内容你可要听仔细了。

So, let's look at these different words for minor injuries, Becca. The listener mentioned 'wound', but that usually sounds quite serious or medical, doesn't it?

Becca
Yes. In everyday conversation, we rarely use 'wound' for a minor injury. It describes more of a deep injury that breaks the skin and takes a while to heal.

Buli
Ah, so a wound is like a cut in that sense?

Becca
Hmm, yes and no. A wound could be any injury that breaks the skin. A cut is specifically a break in the skin caused by a sharp object or forceful impact.

Buli
虽然单词 “wound” 的意思是 “伤口”，但在生活中，我们通常不用 “wound” 来描述一般的小刮小蹭。它指的是那些 “穿透了皮肤表面的，特别是面积偏大、需要较长一段时间才能恢复的伤口”。而问题中提到的单词 “cut” 虽然也可以指 “伤口”，但它却和伤口的大小无关，描述的是 “由尖锐物体所造成的划伤、割伤”。

此外，许多描述伤口的单词也可以用作动词。比如，“wound” 和 “cut” 这两个单词就可以表示 “受伤” 和 “切到，划伤”。

Becca
Interestingly, they're similar in that they both break the skin, and we can use them metaphorically to talk about an emotional injury.

Buli
Ah, so like when I said that my pride was wounded after tripping near the cafe.

Becca
Yes, or when I said that the situation of the job interview cut me deep.

Buli
是的，和在汉语中类似，英语中诸如 “wound” 和 “cut” 等单词不但可以描述物理意义上的 “伤口”，还可以表示 “内心受伤” 或者 “内心的伤口”。比如，我们可以用 “I was wounded by his word” 来表示 “他说的话让我很受伤”。

Becca, are there any other words related to injury or being wounded?

Becca
There are many, of course. For example, we can 'bruise' metaphorically in this way to describe emotional damage, but not to the same extent as wound or cut. And this is because a bruise is a break of the blood vessels under the skin. It's usually not as serious but changes the colour of the skin.

Buli
Like the discolouration on fruit. Also, I heard you use the word 'bump' before.

Becca
Yes. A bump is a raised, swollen area also cause by impact. When I bumped into the glass door, I bumped my head, and now there's a bump! Bumps could also appear as small raises in the skin, like little red spots, usually because of friction to the skin or when we have an allergic reaction to something.

Buli
是的。“Bump” 和 “bruise” 是两个和 “撞，磕碰” 有关的单词。其中，“bump” 既可以指 “撞上” 和 “撞出的包”，也可以指 “过敏时身上起的小红点”。而 “bruise” 通常描述的是 “挫伤”，或者 “被挫伤时出现的淤青”。

不过，在这两个单词中，只有 “bruise” 跟 “wound” 类似，可以用来比喻 “内心受到了伤害”。

Becca
Lastly, scratch and scrape are similar because they're minor injuries. A scratch is a thin, shallow mark caused by something sharp sliding across the skin. And a scrape happens over a wider area and when the skin is worn down, usually from sliding against a hard or rough surface. It's also known as a graze.

Buli
Ouch! They all sound quite unpleasant. 还有两个描述轻伤的单词 “scratch” 和 “scrape” 也十分常见。“Scratch” 指的是 “抓伤、划伤”。和 “cut” 相比，“scratch” 造成的伤口往往更宽一些。“Scratch” 也经常用来描述被小猫小狗等小动物的爪子 “抓伤”。

“Scrape” 指的则是 “擦伤，刮伤”。如果你不小心摔了一跤，膝盖蹭破了皮，那么就可以说 “I fell and scraped my knees”。

Becca
Like what I did when I got off the bus! Oh, let's not talk about that any more… Remember if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!

item.title: 职场沟通中常见的英语缩略词
item.description:
内容简介

“FYI”、“ASAP”、“WFH”、“OOO”……在工作交流中，英语缩略词随处可见。它们不仅能提高沟通效率，也体现了职场英语的语言习惯。除了熟悉的 “FYI” 和 “ASAP”，你知道 “WFH” 和 “OOO” 分别代表什么吗？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Georgie 学习五个英语缩略词以及它们的地道用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。This is Question and Answer of the Week, where we answer your questions about English language, culture and life. My name's Buli, and I've got Georgie here to help me answer this week's question. How are you, Georgie?

Georgie
I'm pretty good, thanks Buli. Just FYI, though, I've got a meeting straight after this recording.

Buli
Right. So you'd like to begin ASAP? We can do that.

Georgie
That would be great. How are you, anyway?

Buli
Yeah, I'm well, thanks. Let's hear this week's question.

Question
我在和外国同事发邮件或者发消息的时候总是看到各种英文缩写，但有时候不知道这些缩写到底是什么意思。除了 “WFH” 和 “FYI”，请问还有哪些缩写在写邮件、发消息或者开会的时候很常见？

Georgie
It's a great question, because we often use these shortcuts to make communications quicker and easier, but if you don't know them, it can be hard to follow what's going on.

Buli
是的。而且不只是文字交流，其实我们在说英语的时候也经常会用到一些缩略词 “acronyms”。缩略词指的是用一个短语或表达的单词首字母来组成一个简短又顺口的新单词。Like when you said 'FYI', Georgie, which means 'for your information'.

Georgie
Yes. When you say 'FYI', the meaning is similar to 'just letting you know'. You're just giving someone information, and often no action is required. Just FYI, Buli, this acronym is usually neutral sounding, but it can sound rude or passive aggressive if you're delivering information you think the person should already know. For example, 'FYI, this information was in the previous email'.

Buli
Ooh, that makes me shudder. “FYI” 的完整说法是 “for your information”。在工作中，这个说法的意思类似于 “请知悉”。当人们用 “FYI” 来引出某条信息的时候，往往是想表达 “我觉得这个信息你需要知道一下，但不需要你马上做什么”。

不过有时候，人们也会先回答对方的问题，然后再用 “FYI” 略带严厉地指出对方原本可以怎么用更简单的方式、更早地获取这些信息，暗示 “这件事你早就应该知道了”。

在节目的一开始，我还用到了 “ASAP” 这个缩略词。“ASAP” 的全称是 “as soon as possible（尽快，越快越好）”。这个词的用法跟副词 “immediately（立刻，马上）” 和 “straightaway（立即，毫不犹豫）” 基本一致。比如，我们可以说 “Can you get that report to me ASAP?” 意思就是 “你能尽快把那份报告给我吗？”

Georgie
Now, the listener also mentioned 'WFH'. That means 'working from home' or 'work from home'. Interestingly, this one is not common in speech because it actually takes longer to say 'WFH' than 'working from home', because the acronym has more syllables. But it is a common shortcut in digital communications. What are some others, Buli?

Buli
Well, I've seen people use 'TBC' and 'TBD'.

Georgie
Oh yeah. 'TBC' means 'to be confirmed', used a lot in scheduling and event planning. It means we might have a rough idea about what's going to happen, but we're waiting for the final details to be decided or confirmed.

Buli
Right. And I know that 'TBD' means 'to be determined' or 'to be decided'.

“TBC” 和 “TBD” 是一对意思非常相近的缩略词，它们分别表示 “to be confirmed” 和 “to be determined or decided”。

这两个缩略词的区别在于，“TBC” 形容那些 “已经基本敲定了，只等最终确认（confirm）” 的工作和事务，而 “TBD” 指的则是那些 “最终方案或选项还有待决定（decide）” 的事情。It's common to say both of these in speech as well, isn't it?

Georgie
It is. Another helpful acronym is 'OOO', meaning 'out of office'. This one you wouldn't say in speech, but it's often written in emails to let colleagues know you're unavailable and may be slow to respond. It could mean you're on holiday, for example, 'I'll be OOO between these dates on annual leave, so please contact this person for urgent matters.'

Buli
Right. Or just that you'll be away from your desk temporarily.

在电子邮件中，“OOO” 也是一个十分常见的缩略词，它的意思是 “out of office（不在办公室）”。要注意的是，其实不只是从短期到长期的休假，任何让人暂时离开工位、不方便联系的事情都可以是 “OOO”，比如，去吃午饭或者临时去医院看病。

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Georgie 正在分享一些在工作场合常见的 “acronyms（缩略词）”。

Georgie
Something that's worth noting about these acronyms is that sometimes the acronym itself takes on a slightly different tone or meaning to the original phrase, especially in speech. For example, saying 'FYI' in speech feels more informal and possibly more friendly than saying 'for your information'.

Buli
Absolutely. 在工作场合中，人们经常会通过选择使用缩略词还是更完整的表达来区分场合和态度。比如，在口语中使用像是 “FYI” 和 “ASAP” 等缩略词往往比使用它们的全称给人的感觉更轻松随意。如果你在口语中用 “as soon as possible” 来催促一个人的话，就比用 “ASAP” 听上去要严肃和着急得多。而在书面语中，使用缩略词的大写还是小写同样会给人不同的感觉。如果你想在提醒对方的同时让自己的语气更加友善、缓和，那么使用小写会是一个不错的选择。

Georgie
Yes. In general, writing words in capital letters often has the connotation of shouting, and therefore aggression. So, you may see people writing acronyms in lowercase letters to soften the tone.

And sometimes, acronyms can be said as full words rather than their individual letters. For example, 'A-S-A-P' is sometimes said as 'ASAP'.

Buli
OK, Georgie, I remember you have another appointment after this, so why don't we finish this programme ASAP?

Georgie
Don't forget that if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你也可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Georgie
Goodbye!

item.title: 辨析英语中三个描述大学课程的词汇：“lecture”、“seminar” 和 “tutorial”
item.description:
内容简介

在许多用英语授课的大学里，特别是在英国大学，课程通常会被分为 “lecture”、“seminar” 和 “tutorial” 等不同形式。对于许多学生来说，除了选择自己感兴趣的课程内容和认可的授课教师外，每门课程的授课形式是否适合自己，也是选课时需要认真考虑的因素之一。听本期节目，跟主持人步理和 Becca 一起了解英语中的 “lecture”、“seminar” 和 “tutorial” 这三种授课形式究竟有什么区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Becca, how are you?

Becca
I'm well thanks, Buli. I've been really enjoying our training over the past few weeks. It's kind of felt like being back at university.

Buli
It has felt that way! And you know what? We have a listener's question asking something just about that.

大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。最近，一位听众向我们发来了这样的问题：

Question
您好，我假期正在进行大学课程的选择。请问在大学里，“seminar”、“lecture” 还有 “tutorial” 这三种授课形式有什么区别呢？

Buli
This is a very interesting question. But, Becca, you've been talking about the training we've been having, haven't you?

Becca
To be honest, I was a little concerned about this training before we started. I was worried that it would feel like one big lecture.

Buli
Yeah, I've attended some training sessions like that, and they can be pretty boring. Luckily, the lady training us is very engaging and gets us to respond to her presentation and talk about our ideas as a group.

Becca
Exactly! She really encourages us to share our thoughts together. We've had some really great conversations about the content we make. In that way, the sessions have felt more like seminars.

Buli
Yes. We can learn from a presentation and then share our ideas. Speaking of content creation, I think I missed the session about short videos for the social media module. Could you share your notes with me?

Becca
Hmm, I could. But I think it would be better to go to our trainer and ask her yourself. She's usually around after the sessions for an hour or so. I'm sure she could give you a tutorial.

Buli
That's a good idea, I'll ask her. Thanks Becca!

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Becca 正在辨析三个在大学教育中常见的课程形式 “lectures”、“seminars” 和 “tutorials”。

正如听众在问题中提到的，在大学里，特别是在英国大学里选课的时候，授课老师通常会在课程的介绍里写明授课的形式。有时，这也是学生们选择自己心仪课程的考虑因素之一。

Becca, let's talk about 'lectures' first.

Becca
Let's! I mentioned that I was a bit worried about the training sessions feeling like a lecture. A 'lecture' is usually a longer session with a professor, or lecturer, standing in front of students, sharing a presentation or giving information about the topic.

Buli
“Lecture” 指的是 “讲座”。和中文里的讲座类似，英国大学的讲座也通常由教师来主讲，基本都是和课程内容有关的 “干货”，没有太多互动性的课堂活动或者练习。

If I were a teacher in university, I would worry about my lectures being boring, because students usually have to actively listen for quite a long time and take a lot of notes.

Becca
Me too. Personally, I would much prefer to teach seminars! Seminars feel more similar to classes because the professor will teach you a little about the topic and then you have to work in pairs or groups to share your thoughts about what you've learnt.

Buli
Yes, they're much more interactive.“Seminar” 在中文里可以解释为 “讨论课，研讨班”。顾名思义，“seminar” 更加注重在课上调动学生的思考和讨论，从而加深彼此对课程内容的理解，产生新的想法。比如，教师可能会先对这节课的主题和核心知识进行简要的介绍，然后再让每位学生结合自己的阅读和了解，自由发言或者进行 “group discussion（小组讨论）”。

Becca
They're also maybe a bit more interesting for some people, as you'll learn not only what the professor is teaching, but also different perspectives from your classmates. Usually, your classmates, and yourself, would have chosen the module to study and so there's a shared interest.

Buli
Yes. The module covers a specific subject and lasts for a set period of time. 在英国大学选课时，不同的课程也会被称为 “modules”，也就是 “课程单元，课程模块”。而在一个课程中的 “一节课” 则可以被称为一个 “session”。

Now, Becca, I missed a session in the module about social media, and you recommended asking for a tutorial?

Becca
So, a tutorial is more of a one-to-one session with your professor, though it can also be done in small groups. It's more focused on deepening understanding through active discussion, reviewing assigned work, and addressing specific learning needs.

Buli
是的。“Tutorial” 指的是 “辅导课”。和主要由教师讲授的 “lecture” 以及学生参与比较多的 “seminar” 比起来，“tutorial” 更多的是一对一的答疑解惑以及教师对学生提交的作业进行详细反馈。除此之外，在学生完成毕业论文或毕业设计时，指导老师对学生进行的专门辅导也可以被称为 “tutorial”。

Becca
Because you missed the session, you have a gap in your knowledge, so I think it would be useful for you to ask for a tutorial.

Buli
Hey, that suits me! I'll ask for a tutorial to catch-up with what I missed.

Becca
Remember if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!

item.title: 谈论 “gardening（园艺）” 时常用的英语词汇和表达
item.description:
内容简介

在生活和工作空间里摆放绿植、鲜花，是不少人的日常习惯。在英国，很多人也热衷于在花园或阳台种植自己喜欢的花草，还会前往当地的 “gardening centre（园艺中心）” 挑选幼苗、种子和各类园艺用品。听节目，跟主持人步理和 Neil 学习与园艺和植物养护相关的英语单词和表达。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Neil
Hey, Buli, do you know anything about the mud stains outside this studio?

Buli
Yeah… Those are probably from my boots. And watch out for your pants, too. Sorry I accidentally put a bag of compost on that chair.

Neil
What?!

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。I'm Buli.

Neil
And I'm Neil. Since I've checked my chair and luckily, everything seems fine, let's hear the question.

Question
你好，我的英国笔友和我一样都喜欢摆弄花花草草，但有时候我不知道怎么给他形容我种东西的方法和过程，比如不同生长阶段的植物啊，花啊怎么说，还有松土和移栽用的小铲子和小耙子之类的工具和使用它们的动作。请问你们可以介绍一些这方面的词汇和表达吗？

Neil
I like this question because I've started to grow things in my garden, so it's good to share the vocabulary about it.

Buli
Yes. Any hobby has its own specialist set of language. Let's learn some of it in this programme.

Neil
Where have you been anyway, Buli? You've never worn boots to the office before.

Buli
Oh, I've just been to the garden centre. I've bought a pot and some seeds. I'm going to try to grow these flowers.

Neil
And you've got the other things you need? A trowel, watering can, a rake perhaps? I see you've got compost at least.

Buli
Yes, I've got all of that. I've even got a big garden fork at home.

Neil
Ah. Well, it definitely sounds like you like gardening!

Buli
Yeah, look at this picture of my garden. Everything is at different stages. There are some tiny seedlings here – you can just see the first green shoots. But if you look at those flowers, they've already got some buds. I just can't wait to see them bloom.

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习和 “gardening（园艺）” 有关的英语表达。其实不只是在宽阔的花园里，哪怕是形容如何在阳台或桌面上养点花花草草，这些单词和表达也都能派上用场。

We've got quite a few gardening words here, so let's go through them.

Neil
Yes. For a start, some of them are related to different stages of growing a plant – 'seed', 'seedling', 'buds' and 'bloom'. A seed is the thing you put in the ground. You plant it. When you start to see the first tiny green stems or shoots above the ground, we can call them seedlings.

Buli
Then as the plants grow, you might start to see buds. These are the round shapes that flowers grow out of.

“Seed（种子）”、“seedling（幼苗）”、“bud（花蕾）” 和 “bloom（花朵）” 四个单词分别对应了植物生长周期中常见的四个阶段和形态。在英语中，“seed”、“bud” 和 “bloom” 这三个单词也可以作动词使用。

Buli
动词 “seed” 的意思是 “播种，种下种子”，而 “bud” 和 “bloom” 分别指的则是花草 “发芽，结出花骨朵” 和 “花朵绽放” 的过程。

We heard some of the tools that you can use to take care of plants as well – a 'trowel', 'rake' and 'fork'.

Neil
Yes, a trowel is a little shovel with a short handle that you can use to dig something small. A rake is like a hard broom with a long handle, but with hard metal teeth. We can use it to help prepare the soil for planting, breaking up big bits of earth. We can also use 'rake' as a verb to describe doing this.

Buli
The other thing we use for breaking up the earth and planting things is a fork – it looks a bit like the thing we use for eating, but it's much bigger!

在照顾花草时，我们也会用到许多特殊的工具。比如，“trowel” 指的就是 “可以单手使用的小铲子，松土用的小手铲”。而需要大面积松土或清扫土地时用到的 “耙子”则可以叫做 “rake”。要注意的是，“rake” 通常指的是那些齿部比较密集的 “耙子”，而只有少数分叉的 “草叉” 或 “园艺叉” 则被称为 “fork”，两者的用途是有些不同的。同时，“rake” 还可以作动词，描述 “用耙子松土、整平土地” 的动作。

顺带一提，和国内的 “花鸟鱼虫市场” 有些类似，在英国，人们也会去 “gardening centre（园艺中心，园艺卖场）” 来选购和园艺有关的种子、植物、工具和装饰品。

Then we had a couple of words to talk about where you grow things. We heard 'pot' and 'compost'.

Neil
So, compost is like soil, but it has nutrients that help plants grow. You can buy it at a garden centre, or you can make your own by keeping things like vegetable cuttings and fruit peel and letting it break down for a few months.

And unlike a cooking pot, a flowerpot is the container that you can grow things in. They are usually round and might have holes in the bottom to let out excessive water. Long and rectangular containers for plants are usually called 'planters'. 

Buli
是的。在英国，“长方形的园艺盆或花园盆” 通常被叫做 “planters”，“圆形的小花盆” 则可以被称为 “pot” 或 “flowerpot”。放在花盆里或者撒在地里帮助植物生长的 “营养土，堆肥” 在英语中被叫做 “compost”。同时，我们也可以用 “compost” 作动词来描述 “制作堆肥” 的过程。

最后，Neil 在节目一开始的对话中还提到了一件十分常见的工具，那就是 “watering can（洒水壶，浇花壶）”。它对应的动作自然就是 “water（浇水）”。

Neil
By the way, all that sounds like a lot of hard work, though, so I prefer to use a hosepipe, which is a long flexible pipe you attach to a tap and use to water your garden.

Buli
That is convenient when you have a lot to water!

希望本期节目能帮到这位喜欢摆弄花草的听众，也祝大家在闲暇时种下的绿植和鲜花都能健康成长，为生活增添一抹清新！

Neil
And remember, if you have a question you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Neil
Goodbye!

item.title: 辨析四个与 “开始” 有关的短语：“kick off”、“get underway”、 “set in” 和 “break out”
item.description:
内容简介

单词 “start” 的意思是 “开始”。“Kick off”、“get underway”、“set in” 和 “break out” 这四个短语也都有 “开始” 的意思。不过，它们适用的场景却各不相同。比赛 “开始了” 应该用哪个短语来表达？一场争执 “爆发了” 又该用哪个？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Becca 一起学习这四个表示 “开始” 的短语及其区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Becca, I can't believe how quickly summer went!

Becca
I know! Before we know it, schools and universities will be starting a new term again.

Buli
That's actually perfect because the question in this programme is all about different expressions meaning 'to start'.

大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。I'm Buli.

Becca
And I'm Becca. Today's question is all about the beginning of things.

Question
你好，我知道 “start” 和 “begin” 都有 “开始” 的意思，但请问 “kick off”、“get underway”、“set in” 和 “break out” 这四个代表 “开始” 的短语有什么区别？如果我想说 “新学期开始了” 用哪个短语最合适呢？

Buli
That's an interesting question. By the way, Becca, when does the new term kick off in the UK?

Becca
Well, in the UK, the new academic year starts in September.

Buli
Oh, it's the same in China. The academic year starts after the summer vacation, so it's usually in September that the new term gets underway.

Becca
Yes, then after a few months, the colder weather starts to set in, and students get to go home for the winter holidays. There's also usually an outbreak of colds and other flu-like illnesses. I remember always being sick when I went home for Christmas.

Buli
Hopefully, we'll avoid an outbreak of colds and flus this year!

Becca
Yes, Buli, let's hope so!

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Becca 正在辨析四个固定短语：“kick off”、“get underway”、“set in” 和 “break out”。

So, they can all be used to say 'something started', but what are the differences?

Becca
Well, let's kick off with 'kick off'! You first asked me when the new term kicks off in the UK. 'Kick off' is an informal expression meaning 'to begin'. It originally comes from football, where the game starts with a kick-off. Nowadays, we use it for all kinds of events. I could say, for example, 'tomorrow's meeting kicks off at nine'.

Buli
I see. So, 'kick-off' can also be a noun. “Kick” 的意思就是 “踢”，因此 “kick off” 原本描述的是足球运动中比赛开始时，一方球员首先把球 “踢出去，开球” 的动作。现在，我们可以用 “kick off” 来表示 “开始或启动一项活动，程序或事件”。并且，加上连字符的 “kick-off” 还可以作名词。

What about the phrase 'get underway'?

Becca
'Get underway' is slightly more formal than 'kick off', and it specifically means 'something has officially started and is now in progress'. So, for example, the academic year usually gets underway in September.

Buli
也就是说，“get underway” 这个短语和 “kick off” 比起来相对更加严肃正式一些。“Get underway” 的意思是 “开始，开始进行，开始实施”。人们通常会用这个短语来描述一项重要或正式的活动 “开始了，开启了”。就比如，一个新学期的开始或者一项重要工程的开工建设。

I think I've heard similar expressions in news reports and official announcements. A reporter might say 'a negotiation or a meeting is underway'.

Becca
Yep, that sounds about right!

Now, we also had 'set in' which we use for things that develop gradually and continue for some time, often without a clear beginning or time boundary. It's often used for weather, seasons, or feelings.

Buli
I see. So, I could say, 'relief sets in as we near the end of this hot summer'.

Becca
A great example, Buli! 

Buli
Thank you, Becca. 和 “get underway” 和 “kick off” 略有不同的是，“set in” 这个短语描述的是 “某个事物逐渐来临，一个事件或情况慢慢开始了”。因此，“set in” 通常搭配的是那些 “并没有一个特别明确的开端，渐渐形成或确立的事物”，比如天气、季节或人的心情等等。

And lastly, what about 'break out'?

Becca
'Break out' is used when something unpleasant or unexpected suddenly starts. We often use it with words like war, fire, violence, disease, or arguments.

Buli
Ah, that's why you used it with the flu.

Becca
Yes. And we can use the similar noun of this phrase 'break out' – 'outbreak'.

Buli
短语 “break out” 和以上三者最大的不同，就是它基本上只能用来描述某个负面的事物 “开始出现了，爆发了”。就比如，我们可以说 “an argument broke out in the meeting room（会议室里爆发了一场争论）” 或者 “a fire broke out in the basement（地下室起火了）”。人们也经常会用到相关的名词 “outbreak” 来指代某件事或事物的 “爆发，突然出现”。

Becca
So, to answer the last part of our listener's question: 'kick off', 'get underway', 'set in' and 'break out' can all mean 'to start', but if you want to describe the start of a new school term, it's best to use 'kick off' or 'get underway'.

Buli
是的。对于这位热心听众提出的问题来说，如果想要表达 “新学期开始了”，那么说 “a new school term got underway” 或者更加轻松和口语化的 “a new school term kicked off” 是在这四个短语中的最佳选择。

Becca
Remember if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!
